yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point kept: the 10 am timing, discomfort keeping it short, the Privy Council, the PMBOK quote, "meetings don't get put off if some team members aren't there", "not a status update for the bosses or stakeholders", the token, "timeboxed to between 5 and 15 minutes", the Scrum section and the three questions.
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "have the team front up every day", "encouraged to rock up", "a chance for team members to have a yarn with each other", "before they turn into too much of a headache", "ask for a hand", "size up progress".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural plain Australian ("The stand-up's especially handy", "pull together to sort out tricky or time-consuming issues"), with "yarns" stretched to work follow-ups: "meant to get follow-up yarns going".
yarn-deadset.register: A real but restrained retelling, noticeably lighter than level 4, much close to the original: "The meetings are usually timeboxed to between 5 and 15 minutes, and happen with everyone standing up".
yarn-deadset.tone: The encyclopedic, explanatory tone is kept in a plainer voice: "The idea is that standing for ages gets uncomfortable, and that keeps the meetings short."
yarn-deadset.flow: Readable, with the original's long sentence still clunky: "The practice also builds closer working relationships through how often it happens, the follow-up yarns it needs and how short it is".
yarn-deadset.variety: "yarn" leaned on: "have a yarn with each other", "get follow-up yarns going", "the follow-up yarns it needs".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the article, headings and references kept: "In Scrum", "[7]".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point kept: "so nobody lets the meeting drag on", the Privy Council, the PMBOK quote, "the meeting doesn't get put off if a few of them aren't there", the token, the timebox, the Scrum section and questions.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "Project Management Institute (PMI) reckons daily stand-up is" fits as colour, "everyone gets wind of any likely hurdles", "how they're tracking towards the sprint goal", "team up with someone".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural ("With those daily commitments on the table", "what work they've got lined up"), with one clumsy construction: "heaps more active an aim than your usual status meeting".
yarn-dinkum.register: A real retelling, a little lighter than level 4: "As a rule the meeting happens at the same time and place every working day."
yarn-dinkum.tone: The explanatory tone holds in a chattier voice: "The thinking is that standing about for ages gets uncomfortable".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Mostly smooth, with "heaps more active an aim" and the repeated "yarns" catching the ear.
yarn-dinkum.variety: "yarn" thrice again ("have a yarn with each other", "get follow-up yarns going", "the follow-up yarns it needs"), otherwise varied: "front up", "gets wind of", "rock up", "lined up".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the article retold, structure and references intact.

unharnessed.meaning: Every point kept: "so the meetings stay short", the Privy Council, PMBOK quote, "the meeting doesn't get put off if a few of 'em aren't there", "not a status report for the bosses or stakeholders", the token, timebox, Scrum section, "Those questions got the flick from the 2020 Scrum Guide." "a much more hands-on aim" shifts "active" slightly.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "any strife coming up", "team up to knock over the tricky or time-chewing problems", "any software development process going", "no rabbiting on", "got the flick"; "hands-on" for "active" bends a little.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian explaining it: "before they turn into a right mess", "chuck in a short comment", "what they reckon they'll be working on till the next one".
unharnessed.register: A full retelling at a good weight, no swearing, within the dial: "It's meant to be quick, less than 15 minutes, so any deep-dive yakking about what's in the way gets held over till the thing's done."
unharnessed.tone: The explanatory, neutral tone comes through in a chattier voice: "One of the big things about it is that it's a chance for the team to have a yarn with each other".
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way, even the long sentence: "Because it happens so often, needs follow-up chats and is kept short, it also gets people working closer together".
unharnessed.variety: Varied, nothing leaned on: "strife", "knock over", "time-chewing", "yarn", "chats", "know-how", "having their say", "rabbiting on", "yakking", "got the flick".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the article, retold, with headings, questions and references kept.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point kept, with many asides. Most react to the original ("So if it's good enough for the King's mob, it's good enough for your lot.", "like the talking stick at school camp", "Save the chinwag for later."), but some add claims: "usually at around 10 am, just before smoko", "your back starts playing up", "where half the room's asleep", and "Back to the drawing board, I s'pose." implies the questions failed.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "sort out the curly or time-consuming issues", "bung it into any software development process you like", "gets wind of the hurdles", "get parked till after it's done".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: A lively Australian voice ("the King's mob", "curly"), with some stock or forced lines: "Now, this one's a ripper.", "Genius.", "Have a crack at saying that standing on one leg."
yarn-troppo.register: A full pub yarn, at or a shade past level 4, no swearing: "Now, this one's a ripper." ... "Short meetings, built in. Genius."
yarn-troppo.tone: A neutral encyclopedia entry turns jokey, even mocking: "where half the room's asleep", "Back to the drawing board, I s'pose."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads lively, but the asides interrupt: "The PMBOK (7th edition) by the Project Management Institute (PMI), and that's a mouthful, reckons".
yarn-troppo.variety: Widely varied: "ripper", "smoko", "playing up", "the King's mob", "Have a crack", "front up", "curly", "bung", "rock up", "chinwag", "parked".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the article, but the jokes crowd the explanation: "And here's the clever bit: standing about for ages gets uncomfortable, your back starts playing up".

engine.register: Untranslated for a level-4 brief: "The discomfort of standing for long periods is intended to keep the meetings short."
engine.tone: The encyclopedic tone is the original's, broken once by the nonsense swap.
engine.flow: Reads as the original, except the broken line: "coordinate efforts to swear blind difficult or time-consuming issues".
engine.variety: One substitution, "swear blind", and nothing else.
engine.essence: Recognisably the article, because it is the article: "Scrum has daily meetings (the daily scrum) for the team to reflect and assess progress towards the sprint goal."

summaries.yarn-dinkum: A natural, faithful retelling a touch light for level 4, with one clumsy line and a leaned-on "yarn".
summaries.unharnessed: The most natural and varied retelling, faithful throughout, at a good level-4 weight.
